newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka troops push into rebel-held north.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka troops push into rebel-held north.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops pushed deeper into Tamil rebel-held territory in the north of the country on Friday, but the military remained quiet about the aim of the four-day old operation, the biggest this year.

A spokesman for the Defence Ministry said guerrillas of the separatist Liberation Tigers of Tamil Ealam (LTTE), who are fighting for a minority Tamil homeland in the north and east, have so far offered no resistance to the advance.
"Altogether, we have gone nearly 18 km (11 miles) into enemy territory," a Defence Ministry spokesman said.

Backed by artillery, air force bombers and tanks and led by elite commando and air-mobile units, the army began the advance from Vavuniya, a key government outpost 220 km (135 miles) north of Colombo, on Tuesday, Sri Lanka's Independence Day.
The LTTE said in a statement seen on Friday that government troops had been attacking civilians in villages in the advance.

The ministry spokesman declined to reveal the exact location of the army units or where they were headed, but military officials in the area said troops were advancing in two flanks, heading north and west from Vavuniya.
The officials, who declined to be named, said one flank had reached a key road junction about 20 km (12 miles) west of Vavuniya.
The road leads to Madhu village dominated by rebel bases and training camps. Madhu houses an historic Christian shrine.
It was not immediately clear if the troops would head towards Madhu or turn north towards the government-held town of Kilinochchi, 70 km (45 miles) to Vavuniya's north.
The Defence Ministry also said the Sri Lankan navy sank a rebel speedboat off the coast of Mannar, west of the the army's offensive, late on Wednesday. There was no word on casualties.
In a statement on their Internet web site, the LTTE accused the government of attacking civilians in the latest offensive.
"Early reports suggest there is already a significant civilian death toll with local families taken by surprise and the young and old completely disoriented," the statement said.

"The unrestrained character of this latest military offensive confirms many observers' fears that an intensive effort to diminish the north-east Tamil population was being prepared by Sri Lanka," the LTTE statement said.
It did not give details of civilian casualties.
"That statement is wrong. The military does not attack villages nor does it kill civilians. We safeguard both," the ministry spokesman said.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the 14-year old conflict but the LTTE says the toll is much higher.
